# `unchecked-slice-reinterpretation`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports nested `@alignCast` and `@ptrCast` operations applied in either order to
a plain slice without an alignment guarantee in its type.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Arbitrary slice storage may be too short or insufficiently aligned for the
destination value. Reinterpreting it as a typed pointer can panic or read beyond
the supplied input.

## When it fires

The rule follows the cast operand to the `.ptr` of a slice binding, directly
or through the operand's own declaration (`const shifted = raw.ptr + offset;`).
Validate the input length and copy bytes into aligned storage before reading the
typed value. Slices carrying an explicit alignment, value-copying APIs, and
functions that take a `mem.Alignment` parameter beside the slice, as allocator
implementations do, are not reported.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const Header = extern struct { magic: u32, len: u32 };

fn parse(raw: []const u8) Header {
    const aligned: *align(@alignOf(Header)) const u8 = @alignCast(@ptrCast(raw.ptr));
    return @as(*const Header, @ptrCast(aligned)).*;
}
```
